Accepted ES c8dc72cf9ec00ab00d6c4a9fcdcea1746c6f1f78 maps NINTENDO_GAMECUBE to RC_CONSOLE_GAMECUBE. Its getCheevosHashFromFile returns the all-zero failure sentinel when generateHashFromFile fails. The wrapper external/libcheevos/cheevos.cpp:156 registers a custom CD reader only; GameCube's hash_disc.c:512 opens the file directly and expects the uncompressed-disc magic at0x1c. No RVZ reader is registered on this path. This is a strong source/runtime match for the missing frontend recognition; it does not prove a failure in standalone Dolphin's in-game achievement support.

Upstream research lead: RetroArch#18316 reports RVZ hashing and current RetroArch has a dedicated cheevos_rvz reader; inspect exact upstream fix/licensing/test coverage before selecting an implementation. https://github.com/libretro/RetroArch/issues/18316 . Source freshness remains required; do not work around this by asking the owner to bulk-convert their library.

Next: synthetic ISO/RVZ equivalence and invalid/truncated controls in the VM, with a bounded reader or an appropriate existing upstream integration; verify frontend/offline indexing and independent Dolphin behavior. Track this confirmed recognition failure within M7 before the next candidate, after current owner-ordered browser/account/copy tasks.

The first format run stopped on an existing baseline UBSan alignment error in libretro-common MD5 (`MD5_SET`, `md5.c:110`) while hashing the official synthetic GameCube input. Original wrapper exit1 is preserved. The baseline and frozen candidate carry the same word-load implementation. The upstream libretro-common source at39eae6ac1c4e4dd809f27cec210ace8d62a5c0a5 retains the same x86/VAX unaligned cast optimization; no matching upstream alignment issue was found in the scoped search. This is C alignment undefined behavior seen under instrumentation, not evidence of an observed handheld crash or a new RVZ regression.

An isolated local ES branch `feature/m7-md5-alignment`, commit314da58d6, replaces that word dereference with memcpy while preserving byte order, plus264 offset/length/split-update checks for independent MD5 comparison. It is source-only: target compile, sanitizer runtime, combined-wrapper regressions and pin promotion remain pending. Frozenbb9e and productionc8dc72 are unchanged. Do not disable alignment sanitization to count the interrupted run as passed.

A separate independent subset passed with the original instrumented candidate: four concurrent RVZ readers, eight open/close rounds each, repeated full/range reads and descriptor-balance assertions; all five byte-for-byte padding vectors agree with the pinned Dolphin implementation. All original processes0/exited, empty sanitizer stderr. This does not supply CHD/DolphinTool format proof or Wii catalog compatibility. Records: current offline VM owner, `sanitizer-subset-host`, `sanitizer-diagnosis-host`, and `sanitizer-reader02-host`.

## Upstream disposition requested — 2026-10-14

> With the work we're doing around Dolphin, is this an upstream issue we need to submit a fix for with this specific file type, or is it something unique on our end in the parsing? Also, if this is a candidate for a smaller patch, we can upstream to ROCKNIX. Let's make a note of that.

Keep three scopes separate:

1. **RVZ frontend recognition/hashing:** the confirmed defect is the EmulationStation/libcheevos reader integration described in this issue, not an established defect in Dolphin's own RVZ decoder or in-game achievement support. Prepare a focused ROCKNIX/EmulationStation contribution after the independent format and sanitizer gates pass. Reuse the appropriate existing upstream reader work and preserve license/credits; do not submit our full fork overlay or unrelated UI/cloud changes.
2. **MD5 alignment:** full-library UBSan caught an unaligned `uint32_t` load in the bundled MD5 fast path, also present at inspected libretro-common file revision 39eae6ac1c4e4dd809f27cec210ace8d62a5c0a5. A separate memcpy-based candidate is committed locally as 314da58d68820a79b26f99a5b6c12f9bb37054d5. Its target compilation and digest/alignment runtime controls remain UNRUN. If those pass, offer the minimal fix to libretro-common first, then carry the reviewed dependency patch where needed. This is not evidence of a Dolphin RVZ defect.
3. **Dolphin save-path preservation/recovery:** #581 concerns distro launch/storage integration. Compare the small fix with ROCKNIX's current scripts and propose it there if their equivalent flow is affected. The current path-layout change only inserts a display newline; it does not change any path on disk.

Follow-up acceptance: [ ] exact target repository/current upstream comparison; [ ] minimal content-only patch and attribution; [ ] relevant synthetic/format/sanitizer evidence; [ ] upstream issue/PR link or explicit duplicate/already-fixed disposition. No upstream submission has been made. No owner ROM, save or credential data is needed.

Correction: the original routing note called the MD5 source rcheevos. The inspected file is libretro/libretro-common `utils/md5.c`; that is the first upstream target. Proxy RVZ tracing and the explicit contribution rule are tracked in #583.
